songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World
It's All Over Now Baby Blue

supporting_acts: Jack Casady, Jorma Kaukonen, and Joey Covington

ai_show_review.summary: Pedal‑steel gems, soaring Dark Star > St Stephen > The Eleven, tight jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The set bursts with Jerry’s pedal‑steel on Slewfoot and Dire Wolf, while the second half erupts into a seamless Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven. Casey Jones is extended and energetic, making this one of the stronger late‑’69 outings.
ai_show_review.review: On June 27 1969 at Santa Rosa’s Veterans Auditorium the Dead delivered a show that straddles their folk‑country roots and emerging psychedelic flights. Jerry Garcia shines on pedal steel throughout Slewfoot* and Dire Wolf, adding a plaintive twang that dovetails with Bob Weir’s enthusiastic lead vocal on Dire Wolf. The first half rolls through country‑leaning numbers before the band launches into an unforgettable Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven sequence – Phil Lesh’s Lovelight‑rich bass anchors the jam while Mickey and Bill lock into a tight, propulsive groove after a looser opening. Casey Jones receives a roomy, extended treatment that highlights the group’s growing confidence, and the encore “It’s All Over Now Baby Blue” rounds out the set with a bittersweet finish. Overall the performance is relaxed yet adventurous, offering several high‑water marks for any Deadhead collector.

best_recording.reason: Clear soundboard feed with good balance, minimal hiss and glitches, capturing the pedal‑steel textures and jam dynamics especially on Dark Star > Saint Stephen > The Eleven.

key_highlights: Jerry’s standout pedal‑steel work on Slewfoot* and Dire Wolf
Extended, seamless Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven jam
Bob’s enthusiastic lead vocal on Dire Wolf
song_highlights: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

band_performance.Jerry: Featured heavily on pedal steel for Slewfoot*, Dire Wolf and early Casey Jones; praised for tone, creativity and adding a distinctive country‑psychedelic flavor.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a strong Lovelight‑rich bass line in Dark Star; occasional timing slip noted early in the set but overall solid foundation throughout the jams.
band_performance.Bob: Takes lead vocals on Dire Wolf with an enthusiastic, country‑style delivery that many reviewers cite as a highlight; contributes to the song’s energy.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums sound loose on opening tunes but lock in tightly for the later psychedelic sections, driving the Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven sequence.
band_performance.Billy: Initially a bit loose and loses time on Dupree's Diamond Blues, then tightens up dramatically for the extended jams, delivering solid rhythmic support.

must_listen_sequences: It's All Over Now Baby Blue
